mainEntity.name: Does the Renters’ Rights Act apply to Airbnb lets?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Act’s main changes are aimed at assured tenancies, where someone lives in the property as their home. Genuine holiday and short-term lets are generally not assured tenancies, so they are treated differently. London’s 90-night rule for whole-home short lets still applies.

mainEntity.name: Can I switch from a long-term tenant to short lets?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only once the tenancy has ended lawfully. Since section 21 was abolished, that means the tenant gives notice or you use one of the legal possession grounds. Plan the switch around the tenancy, not the other way round.

mainEntity.name: Is serviced accommodation a middle ground?

acceptedAnswer.text: For many London properties, yes. Longer stays for corporate guests, contractors and people relocating can fill the nights that short lets cannot use under the 90-night rule. Read how short-term let management works to compare.

mainEntity.name: What areas does Ichiban Stays operate in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ichiban Stays manages a curated portfolio of serviced apartments across the UK, including some of London's most central and sought-after neighbourhoods.

mainEntity.name: What is a serviced apartment?

acceptedAnswer.text: A serviced apartment is a fully furnished apartment available for short or extended stays, combining the space and privacy of a home with hotel-style services such as housekeeping and guest support.

mainEntity.name: How is a serviced apartment different from a hotel room?

acceptedAnswer.text: Serviced apartments offer more space, a separate living area, and a private kitchen, making them better suited to longer stays or guests who want independence without sacrificing hospitality-standard service.

mainEntity.name: How long can guests stay with Ichiban Stays?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ichiban Stays accommodates both short stays and extended stays, making its apartments suitable for holidays, business trips, and longer relocations to London.

mainEntity.name: Which London neighbourhoods can I stay in with Ichiban Stays?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ichiban Stays' portfolio spans central and well-connected London neighbourhoods, giving guests easy access to the city's main parks, shopping, and business districts.

mainEntity.name: How do I book with Ichiban Stays?

acceptedAnswer.text: Guests can get in touch directly via contact@ichibanstays.com or +44 7572 190291 to check availability and arrange a booking.

mainEntity.name: How does Ichiban Stays price its apartments?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ichiban Stays uses dynamic, data-driven pricing to keep rates responsive to demand, alongside its own in-house property management system.

mainEntity.name: How does short-term property management work?

acceptedAnswer.text: You provide the property; the management company handles listing it, pricing it, managing guests, cleaning between stays, maintenance and compliance, with regular reporting back to the landlord.

mainEntity.name: Is there an upfront fee?

acceptedAnswer.text: No — Ichiban Stays has no upfront fees to get started.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to be present or available during guest stays?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A dedicated manager and the wider team handle guest communication, check-in/check-out and any issues during a stay.

mainEntity.name: Do I need planning permission for a short let in London?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whole-property short lets in London are currently capped at 90 nights per calendar year without planning permission.

mainEntity.name: Is my property and data handled securely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — data is kept secure throughout the management of a property.
